previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after developing chest pain and hypotension during a dialysis session. Her symptoms were brief, without diaphoresis or ECG changes, and cardiac enzymes remained negative, ruling out myocardial infarction. Hypotension was attributed to excessive fluid removal during dialysis, leading to demand ischemia. She received a fluid bolus, which stabilized her blood pressure. Nephrology consultation recommended a dry weight of 53 kg and temporary discontinuation of antihypertensive medications until reassessment at the next dialysis session. Her rhythm was managed with continued amiodarone and anticoagulation. Chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities with interval improvement, and blood cultures were negative. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to hold certain blood pressure medications, resume others based on dialysis team guidance, and take amiodarone daily, along with close follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ with shortness of breath.  Evaluate for CHF.

No prior examinations.

as evidenced by increased interstitial markings and perihilar haze.  There is
also more diffuse opacity throughout the right lung which may represent
alveolar edema, and a dense consolidation in the right middle and lower lobes
which is consistent with pneumonia.  The heart is nearly completely obscured.
The aortic contour is normal.

IMPRESSION:  Moderate pulmonary edema and large consolidation of the right

FINDINGS:  Newly placed right PICC terminates approximately 1 cm below the
cavoatrial junction.

The cardiac silhouette is moderately enlarged.  There is a new right lower
lobe opacity, concerning for pneumonia.  There is mild interstitial edema
developed in the interval.  There is an opacity in the left retrocardiac area,
which may represent atelectasis or consolidation.  There is no pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Malpositioned PICC.  Recommend retraction by 3 cm for tip location in the
distal superior vena cava.
2.  Right lower lobe consolidation, concerning for pneumonia.  Left
retrocardiac opacity may represent pneumonia or atelectasis.
3.  Mild interstitial edema.
